questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Second Derivative of a Parametric Curve
questions.problem: A curve is defined by the parametric equations $x={t}^{2}-2,\,y=2{t}^{4}+5$ where $t$ is a real number. Calculate $\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}.$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the first derivative, we will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{{y}^{′}(t)}{{x}^{′}(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=2t,\,{y}^{′}(t)=8{t}^{3}.
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{8{t}^{3}}{2t}=4{t}^{2}.
$$

To compute the second derivative, we can use the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(\frac{dy}{dx})}{(\frac{dx}{dt})}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(4{t}^{2})}{2t} \\  & =\frac{8t}{2t} \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Second Derivative of a Parametric Curve
questions.problem: A curve is defined by the parametric equations $x=-\operatorname{cos}⁡t+3,\,y=2\operatorname{sin}⁡t-1.$ Calculate $\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}.$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the first derivative, we will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{{y}^{′}(t)}{{x}^{′}(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,{y}^{′}(t)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t.
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{2\operatorname{cos}⁡t}{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}=2\operatorname{cot}⁡t.
$$

To compute the second derivative, we can use the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(\frac{dy}{dx})}{(\frac{dx}{dt})}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(2\operatorname{cot}⁡t)}{\operatorname{sin}⁡t} \\  & =-\frac{2{csc}^{2}⁡t}{\operatorname{sin}⁡t} \\  & =-2{csc}^{3}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Derivative of a Parametric Curve at a Given Point
questions.problem: A curve has parametric equations $x=\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)+4,\,y=-4\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t).$ Given that $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=4\operatorname{tan}⁡(3t),$ calculate $\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}$ at the point where $t=\frac{\pi }{9}.$
questions.worked_solution:
To compute $\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}},$ we can use the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(\frac{dy}{dx})}{(\frac{dx}{dt})}.\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that $\frac{dy}{dx}=4\operatorname{tan}⁡(3t),$ and we can calculate $\frac{dx}{dt}$ as follows:

$$
\frac{dx}{dt}=\frac{d}{dt}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)+4)=3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t).
$$

Substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(4\operatorname{tan}⁡(3t))}{3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)} \\  & =\frac{12{sec}^{2}⁡(3t)}{3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)} \\  & =4{sec}^{3}⁡(3t).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate at $t=\frac{\pi }{9},$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}{|}_{t=\pi /9} & =4{sec}^{3}⁡(3\cdot \frac{\pi }{9}) \\  & =\frac{4}{{cos}^{3}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})} \\  & =\frac{4}{{(\frac{1}{2})}^{3}} \\  & =32.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Derivative of a Parametric Curve at a Given Point
questions.problem: A curve has parametric equations $x={t}^{2}-10,\,y=4{t}^{6}+5.$ Given that $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=12{t}^{4},$ calculate $\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}$ at the point where $t=1.$
questions.worked_solution:
To compute $\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}},$ we can use the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(\frac{dy}{dx})}{(\frac{dx}{dt})}.\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that $\frac{dy}{dx}=12{t}^{4},$ and we can calculate $\frac{dx}{dt}$ as follows:

$$
\frac{dx}{dt}=\frac{d}{dt}({t}^{2}-10)=2t.
$$

Substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(12{t}^{4})}{2t} \\  & =\frac{48{t}^{3}}{2t} \\  & =24{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate at $t=1,$ and we get

$$
{\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}|}_{t=1}=24\cdot {1}^{2}=24.
$$

questions.worked_solution:
To compute $\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}},$ we can use the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(\frac{dy}{dx})}{(\frac{dx}{dt})}.\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that $\frac{dy}{dx}=3{e}^{4t},$ and we can calculate $\frac{dx}{dt}$ as follows:

$$
\frac{dx}{dt}=\frac{d}{dt}({e}^{2t})=2{e}^{2t}
$$

Substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{dt}(3{e}^{4t})}{2{e}^{2t}} \\  & =\frac{12{e}^{4t}}{2{e}^{2t}} \\  & =6{e}^{2t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate at $t=1,$ and we get

$$
\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}\,{|}_{t\,=\,1}=6{e}^{2(1)}=6{e}^{2}.
$$
